title: Roblox 將「青少年文明與福祉委員會」擴展至南美洲
summary: Applications Now Open Across Argentina, Brazil, Canada, Chile, Colombia, Mexico, Peru, and the U.S.
body_text: 分享 安全與文明 社群 Roblox 將「青少年文明與福祉委員會」擴展至南美洲 現已開放阿根廷、巴西、加拿大、智利、哥倫比亞、墨西哥、秘魯及美國各地的申請 發佈者 塔米·巴烏米克（Tami Bhaumik），文明與夥伴關係副總裁 發佈日期 2026年7月21日 隨著 Roblox 的用戶群不斷擴大， 節奏明快且畫質精良的遊戲 也吸引了越來越多的青少年與年輕成人，要滿足他們的需求，就必須讓他們的聲音被聽見。 正因如此，我們於 2024 年成立了首屆「 青少年理事會」 。鑑於 Roblox 玩家社群中有 80% 來自美國以外地區，讓世界各地的年輕人參與其中，能為我們帶來關於文化需求的真實洞見。這不僅有助於讓我們的安全措施與產品功能在當地產生共鳴，同時也賦能新一代的數位福祉倡導者。 今年的「文明與福祉青少年委員會」將擴大招募範圍，除加拿大、墨西哥和美國外，亦將納入來自阿根廷、巴西、智利、哥倫比亞和秘魯的青少年。年齡介於 13 至 17 歲的用戶 可由此處申請 加入下一屆委員會，任期為 2026 年 10 月至 2027 年 6 月。申請現已開放，截止時間為太平洋夏令時間（PDT）8 月 18 日午夜。 我們今年稍早亦宣布成立首屆亞太地區青少年委員會，並 持續徵求 來自泰國、越南、馬來西亞、新加坡及印尼的 申請者 。 「當我們的產品以及安全與福祉計畫能融入玩家的聲音時，這些內容便會更加堅實且真實，」Roblox 青少年參與事務資深專案經理安德烈斯·庫埃沃（Andres Cuervo）表示。「我們正在尋找年輕領袖，特別是那些對數位福祉充滿熱忱的人士，希望他們能分享見解，並協助我們持續成為線上安全與文明行為的全球領導者。」 青少年理事會的影響力 2026 年青少年委員會 匯聚了來自北美各地、年齡介於 14 至 17 歲的 20 位用戶。成員們針對「 Roblox Kids 」 和「Roblox Select」帳戶 以及新 聊天 工具等功能提出建議，並與 Roblox 安全、行銷及工程部門的高層進行交流。 該委員會協助制定了 《Roblox 社群準則》的青少年指南 ——採用淺顯易懂的語言撰寫，以幫助年幼用戶理解平台規則。我們也採用相同的語言風格，簡化了遊戲內的 檢舉流程 。 成員們還與媒體素養組織合作，共同製作了 Roblox 的第二支數位福祉公益廣告，並為「 心理健康意識月」 打造了一個全新的 青少年福祉專頁 。 Teen Council members collaborated with media literacy organizations on a digital well-being public service announcement. 「擔任青少年理事會成員的經歷證明，當我們被賦予發言權時，青少年的見解能產生多大的影響力，」2026 年青少年理事會成員索菲亞表示。「Roblox 確實為我們創造了空間，讓我們能以倡議者和問題解決者的身分，感受到自身的力量。」 「每次會議中，我們都會聽到新加入的 Roblox 團隊成員迫切希望聽取我們對他們工作的反饋——而之後我們也親眼見證了我們的反饋對最終上線產生了多大的影響，」理事會成員瑪吉說道。 如何申請 現年 13 至 17 歲且居住於阿根廷、巴西、加拿大、智利、哥倫比亞、墨西哥、秘魯或美國的用戶 ，現可點擊此處申請 加入 Roblox 2027 年青少年理事會。亞太地區理事會的申請者 請點擊此處申請 。 所有候選人必須精通英語，並取得家長同意方可申請。申請截止時間為 8 月 18 日太平洋夏令時間（PDT）午夜前。

title: Interface Recognized by Newsweek as One of America’s Greenest Companies for 2026
summary: Interface, Inc. the global flooring solutions company and leader in sustainability, announced that Newsweek named it one of America’s Greenest Companies of 2026. The recognition acknowledges the manufacturer’s 30-year history as a sustainability leader, continued carbon reduction progress, and commitment to be carbon negative by 2040. Interface is the only flooring company on the list for the second year in a row.
body_text: Interface Recognized by Newsweek as One of America’s Greenest Companies for 2026 ATLANTA – November 5, 2025 – Interface, Inc. (NASDAQ: TILE), the global flooring solutions company and leader in sustainability, announced that Newsweek named it one of America’s Greenest Companies of 2026. The recognition acknowledges the manufacturer’s 30-year history as a sustainability leader, continued carbon reduction progress, and commitment to be carbon negative by 2040. Interface is the only flooring company on the list for the second year in a row. Newsweek cites the manufacturer’s 1.5ºC-aligned 2030 science-based targets as proof that its climate commitments are in line with the level of action needed to limit the increase in global temperature. The 2030 targets are third-party validated by the Science Based Targets initiative (SBTi) and represent an important milestone toward the company’s carbon negative by 2040 goal. Interface’s targets commit to reductions over an 11-year period, from 2019 to 2030. After just five years, it has already passed the halfway point toward each target, signifying that the company is ahead of pace to achieve its 2030 climate goals. Interface continues to launch and market new innovations that align with its ‘all in’ commitment to be carbon negative by 2040. These advancements are made possible by repurposing former carbon offset investments into projects that accelerate carbon reduction and carbon storage. Two recent achievements include the introduction of the first-ever carbon negative rubber prototype and the integration of captured carbon into its U.S. and European carpet tile manufacturing processes. Both represent Interface’s continued investment in new raw materials and other innovative solutions to help avoid, reduce, and store more carbon across its own products and operations, and throughout its supply chain. “Being named one of America’s Greenest Companies shows that our ‘all in’ commitment is resonating,” said Laurel Hurd, CEO of Interface. “Our approach is simple: avoid, reduce, and store more carbon wherever we can. And we want to inspire others to join us, so together we create a ripple effect for an even bigger impact. After 30 years, we’ve proven that a flooring company can succeed without compromising the planet. If we can do it, anyone can.” The awards program, part of Newsweek's annual ranking in collaboration with Plant-A Insights and GIST Impact, is in its third year. The list highlights public and private U.S. companies dedicated to reducing their environmental impact and addressing the climate crisis. Eligible companies are evaluated and scored on more than 25 parameters related to greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, water use, waste generation, and sustainability data disclosure and commitments. Each company must also meet the European Union's sustainability standards and evaluate Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) issues, including biodiversity, climate change, and human rights. For more information about the Newsweek America's Greenest Companies 2026 ranking, click here . About Interface Interface, Inc., (NASDAQ: TILE) is a global flooring solutions company and sustainability leader, offering an integrated portfolio of carpet tile and resilient flooring products that includes Interface® carpet tile and LVT, nora® rubber flooring, and FLOR® premium area rugs for commercial and residential spaces. Made with purpose and without compromise, Interface flooring brings more sophisticated design, more performance, more innovation, and more climate progress to interior spaces. A decades-long pioneer in sustainability, Interface remains “all in” on becoming a regenerative business. Today, the company is focusing on carbon reductions, not offsets, as it works toward achieving its verified science-based targets by 2030 and its goal to become a carbon negative enterprise by 2040. Learn more about Interface at interface.com , nora by Interface at nora.com , FLOR at FLOR.com , and the company’s sustainability journey at interface.com/sustainability . Follow us on Facebook , Instagram , LinkedIn , X , and Pinterest .

body_text: Invesco Mortgage Capital Inc. July 2026 Dividend Announcement and June Financial Update Company Release - 7/15/2026 Download the PDF version PDF Format (opens in new window) ATLANTA , July 15, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Invesco Mortgage Capital Inc. (NYSE: IVR) (the "Company") today announced that the Company declared a cash dividend of $0.12 per share of common stock for the month of July 2026. The dividend will be paid on August 14, 2026 to stockholders of record at the close of business on July 27, 2026, with an ex-dividend date of July 27, 2026. Financial Highlights as of June 30, 2026 Total investment portfolio including TBAs of $8.2 billion Unrestricted cash and unencumbered investments of $548.3 million Total repurchase agreement borrowings of $6.2 billion Estimated book value per common share of $8.03(1) Debt-to-equity ratio of 6.3x and economic debt-to-equity ratio of 7.5x(2) (1) Estimated book value per common share as of June 30, 2026 is calculated as total stockholders' equity less the liquidation preference of the Company's Series C Preferred Stock ($168.6 million), divided by total common shares outstanding of 102.4 million. (2) Debt-to-equity ratio is calculated in accordance with U.S. GAAP as the ratio of total repurchase agreement borrowings to total stockholders' equity. Economic debt-to-equity ratio is a non-GAAP financial measure and is calculated as the ratio of total repurchase agreement borrowings and TBAs at implied cost basis ($1.2 billion as of June 30, 2026) to total stockholders' equity. Refer to the section titled "Economic Debt-to-Equity Ratio" below for additional information. The Company includes these types of TBAs at implied cost basis in its measure of leverage because a forward contract to acquire Agency RMBS in the TBA market carries similar risks to Agency RMBS purchased in the cash market and funded with on-balance sheet liabilities. The Company believes that presenting its economic debt-to-equity ratio, when considered together with its U.S. GAAP financial measure of debt-to-equity ratio, provides information that is useful to investors in understanding how management evaluates at-risk leverage and gives investors a comparable statistic to those of other mortgage real estate investment trusts who also invest in TBAs and present a similar non-GAAP measure of leverage.
